cards.claim: The prior assessment (BAML is a library for application code that calls models) fits BAML v0, which the project now calls legacy. The current README presents BAML as a general-purpose language with a Rust-like type system, runtime types, typed errors, green threads, a built-in tests/eval framework and an agent stdlib. It can also be called from TS/Py/Go/C#/Java. The v0 docs banner says v1 is a separate language with its own docs. The homepage calls it Turing-complete and pre-1.0. The README no longer mentions SAP, a playground or providers.
cards.evidence: README bullet list; the 'BAML v0 / legacy' banner on every v0 docs page; homepage and new.boundaryml.com wording ('currently pre-1.0'). No benchmarks or measured results are given for any v1 claim.
cards.first_guess: Amend the prior assessment. The choice is not 'adopt a library' but 'legacy v0 in maintenance vs a pre-1.0 v1 language'. Neither is an install candidate for this harness. Keep BAML as a source of ideas (R-05 to R-12) and change no harness file.

cards.source_title: GitHub API: BoundaryML/baml repository metadata (plus CHANGELOG.md and release tags)
cards.claim: Facts. 9,475 stars, 511 forks, licence Apache-2.0, runtime language Rust (the v1 repo has crates bex_vm and bex_sap, the SAP parser). Created 2023-10-06, pushed 2026-11-04, default branch canary, 4,213 commits. Open issues: 230 by issue search (372 on the repo counter, which includes PRs). Cadence: CHANGELOG.md lists about 46 numbered releases from 0.90.0 (2025-06-14) to 0.226.3 (2026-10-27), but only about 9 since 2026-04-14. The latest, 0.226.3, is a TLS/CA security patch. The v1 toolchain ships separately as tags baml-language-<ver>-nightly.<date>.<letter>. Seen: 0.15.1 nightlies on 2026-07-27 (two builds about 2 hours apart) and 0.23.1 nightlies on 2026-10-31 and 2026-11-02. Windows: the nightly assets include x86_64 and aarch64 pc-windows-msvc zips and baml_cffi DLLs. The v0 changelog has repeated Windows path fixes (0.71.0, 0.207.0, 0.212.0).
cards.evidence: Repo metadata fields from the API (stargazers_count 9475, license, language Rust, pushed_at). Release count is my own tally of CHANGELOG headings as relayed by the fetch tool and may omit entries. The release list itself was too large to count.
cards.first_guess: A very active, permissively licensed project, but v1 is pre-1.0 with several nightlies a week and v0 is slowing. Anything adopted would have to be pinned. Windows is a supported target. Nothing to wire in; this is context for the owner.

cards.quote: Injecting your function schemas into the prompt, as BAML does.
cards.claim: BAML does not use provider tool or structured-output APIs. The schema goes into the prompt through ctx.output_format(), and the reply is repaired by SAP. Tool choice is a union return type, and BAML never executes the tool. Issue #875 ('Integrate directly with structured outputs', 2024-08-13) is still open, and the v1 agent skill still tells agents to put ctx.output_format() in prompts. Our Workflow schema option does the opposite: a forced StructuredOutput tool call, validated at the tool layer, with the model retrying on mismatch.
cards.evidence: Docs statement, the still-open issue #875, and the v1 SKILL.md instruction. No measurement of prompt-based vs tool-forced output on current models is given.
cards.first_guess: No change to the harness. It is a useful named contrast for the design doc: we get reject-and-retry from the tool layer rather than repair (see R-05 for what repair costs).

cards.source_date: approx. 2024-09 (page says about two years old; cites gpt-4o-2024-08-06)
cards.claim: The vendor says prompting plus SAP beats native function calling on the Berkeley Function-Calling Benchmark. It claims it is more accurate, cheaper and 'easily 2-4x faster' than strict function calling. The docs page why-baml.md lists about 92-93% for GPT-3.5 and GPT-4o and 91.7% for Claude 3 Haiku. The authors also concede that the original prompting method fails to parse on the newest model, and that BAML 'will soon support the tool APIs'.
cards.evidence: Vendor-run benchmark on 2024-era models. The blog's results table did not render, no sample size or method is stated on the page, and the why-baml numbers carry no methodology. The authors' own footnote says no model can reach 100% on this data.
cards.first_guess: Do not treat it as evidence for or against our forced-StructuredOutput approach. The models are generations old and the method is unpublished. If the owner ever wants a measured comparison, that would be a separate experiment this sweep does not propose.

cards.source_title: Issue #4590: SAP silently discards array elements it cannot coerce (baml run exits 0 with fewer rows)
cards.quote: SAP silently discards array elements it cannot coerce
cards.claim: A lenient, repairing parser turns a schema violation into missing data. In the reproduction, a Row[] with one row missing a required date returns only the good row, exit code 0, and no signal on any channel. The same family is open elsewhere: #1859 (2025-04-25) asks for alternatives to silently dropping invalid list values, #4790 (2026-09-09) reports a whitespace-dependent drop, #3307 (2026-03-30) reports an intermittent empty list, and #3289 reports that a failed @@assert error says only 'Assertions failed.' with empty causes. The reporter asks for a count and path of discarded elements, an opt-in strict mode, and the raw model text on the result.
cards.evidence: Single-reporter reproduction with a control run; 6 comments, but maintainer replies were not visible in the fetched text. The sibling issues are separate reports. The 'repair loses data silently' pattern is independently visible in several of them.
cards.first_guess: Our tool layer rejects rather than repairs, so the exposure is limited to our own script post-processing. Add one rule to §5: any step that filters, de-duplicates or normalises a returned array must report received vs kept counts and the reason for each drop. A verifier then compares asked vs returned. This matches the existing 'never fabricate to fill' stance.

cards.source_title: Testing functions (BAML docs, v0), read together with the Checks and Asserts page
cards.quote: The first failing assert will halt
cards.claim: BAML splits output constraints into two tiers. @check records a named pass/fail status and still returns the value, and all checks are evaluated. @assert is hard: the value is excluded or an error is raised, and chained asserts stop at the first failure. Test blocks can carry @@check and @@assert, and expose the result, earlier checks and latency_ms to later expressions.
cards.evidence: Two docs pages (testing-functions.md and guide/baml-advanced/checks-and-asserts.md). Both carry the v0-legacy banner. No usage data.
cards.first_guess: Name two classes of rule in the §5 contracts. Schema-enforced rules (enums, required fields, patterns) are hard via StructuredOutput. Script-computed checks are recorded as fields that travel to the judge without rejecting, for example quote_is_substring_of_source or word_count_le_15. Because code computes them, they fit the rule that verifiers get claim and evidence only.

cards.source_title: baml-core SKILL.md (agent skill shipped inside the BAML repo)
cards.claim: In the v1 agent loop, 're-ask with a correction when the reply won't parse' is its own budget (schema_attempts), separate from max_steps, and those retries do not count as steps. A run returns ai.RunResult { value, journal, usage }, so retry and usage data is visible to the caller. Our StructuredOutput retry is the same mechanism, but the retry count is invisible to the script.
cards.evidence: Signature and prose in a 51 KB skill file, relayed by the fetch tool. No data on how often schema retries fire.
cards.first_guess: Ask whether agent() exposes attempt or retry counts. If it does, record them per brief, because a brief that bounces off its schema often is a cheap regression signal for (b). If it does not, do nothing. Nothing to build from this card alone.

cards.claim: BAML renders the return type into the prompt as a compact class notation. @description and @alias shape what the model sees, and the page claims about 180 tokens of JSON Schema become about 35. Newer knobs in the changelog: quote class keys (0.215.0), render_null_as (0.223.0) and a toon Jinja filter (0.214.0). Open requests ask for YAML/XML/TSV output (#2409) and flatter schemas (#2609).
cards.evidence: One illustrative example on a vendor page; no corpus or measurement. Changelog entries and open feature requests confirm the knobs exist and that users want them.
cards.first_guess: Token cost is not our problem, since our schema rides in the tool definition. The transferable part is descriptions. Check that every property and every enum member in the §5 schemas (verdict, severity, evidence_kind and so on) carries a one-line description of what the value means, as @description does. Low cost, easy to review by reading the schema.

cards.quote: do not rely on live LLM calls in e2e tests
cards.claim: The project tests its LLM surface without a live model. Parsing is tested by passing a canned string to the generated parse companion. ARCHITECTURE.md says every LLM function desugars into separate companions (spec, render_prompt, build_request, parse, stream). The shipped skill tells agents to inspect requests with build_request, replay saved replies with parse, and use a fake client. Prompt rendering, request building and parsing are separable and testable offline.
cards.evidence: Contributor guide, architecture doc and skill file, all read. Describes practice, not measured effect.
cards.first_guess: A route to brief tests with no model calls. (1) Make brief assembly a pure JS function and assert invariants on it: CONTEXT block present verbatim, no tier word, schema required is a subset of properties, enums non-empty. (2) Replay tests: feed saved real StructuredOutput payloads from past runs through the schema and the judge's post-checks. Both catch hand-edit regressions at zero model cost. Neither needs BAML.

cards.quote: Test prompts 10x faster, right in your IDE
cards.claim: The v0 tooling shows the full rendered prompt, multimodal assets and API request in a playground before any call. Test cases are saved for regression, and baml-cli test --parallel N runs them concurrently. The README's '2 minutes to 5 seconds' example is illustrative. Issue #5322 (2026-10-20) shows the preview path breaking in v1 nightlies ('Function not found: X$render_prompt').
cards.evidence: README wording and the docs claim of testing 'without API calls or token costs'. There are no measurements, and an open bug shows the preview is fragile in the new line.
cards.first_guess: A dry-run switch in Workflow scripts: a flag that makes the script return the fully assembled prompts and schemas instead of calling agent(). A brief edit then reviews as a text diff before any spend. It is a script-only change with no new dependency. Whether it is worth doing depends on how often briefs are hand-edited.

cards.claim: baml-cli optimize --beta (v0, 0.215.0 or later) runs reflective prompt evolution scored by the project's own tests, using @@assert and @@check as the objective. An LLM proposes candidates. It may rewrite prompt text and type descriptions or aliases but never field names. The user picks the candidate. Limits: one function at a time, no workflows, all failures count equally so a transient 500 looks like a prompt failure, and the default optimizer uses Claude (needs ANTHROPIC_API_KEY).
cards.evidence: Docs page only, marked beta. No published results.
cards.first_guess: Premature, because we have no scored fixtures (R-09 comes first). Keep the limits as design rules for any future brief tuning: separate infrastructure failures from content failures when scoring, forbid edits to schema field names, and have a judge or the owner choose the candidate. Not an install candidate.

cards.source_title: BAML skills README (agent skills compiled into baml-cli)
cards.claim: BAML ships its agent guidance (skills/baml-core/SKILL.md, about 51 KB) inside the CLI binary. `baml agent install` writes it into a project, so guidance version equals toolchain version. The homepage says the guidance is 'matched to the project's BAML version', and a separate baml-skill repo is kept only for older toolchains. `baml describe` gives AST-aware code discovery for agents.
cards.evidence: Skills README plus the new.boundaryml.com description of baml agent install. No data on whether it reduces agent errors. The README does not name the individual skills, so the install behaviour rests on the homepage text.
cards.first_guess: For tools/ks, a `ks guide` subcommand that prints the usage contract generated from the same command definitions as the CLI, plus a test that every subcommand appears in it. No model involved. It stops the tool's agent-facing instructions drifting from its behaviour, the same drift CLAUDE.md warns about.

cards.quote: BAML example code used in the Documentation Tutorials
cards.claim: The example shapes, judged from folder names only, are typed extraction and automation (extract-anything, form-filler, survey-answerer, blog-analyzer), a chatbot, MCP servers in Node and Python, web starters (Next.js, Nuxt, Svelte), an AWS Lambda app, and OpenAPI starters for Python/FastAPI, Go, Java, PHP, Ruby and Rust. No example resembles a multi-agent orchestrator or an agent-harness script.
cards.evidence: Folder listing (25 folders, 143 stars, 142 commits). The README says nothing about each project's purpose, so my reading of each shape is inferred from names.
cards.first_guess: Harness: nothing to take. FixFlow product (none planned): the nearest shape is typed extraction behind FastAPI, for example structured intake from free-text customer messages. That is a product idea for the owner, not a plan; FixFlow has no LLM features.

cards.source_title: Open issues mentioning 'anthropic' in BoundaryML/baml (GitHub issue search, 11 results)
cards.quote: allow using claude code as a client<llm>
cards.claim: Anthropic is a supported provider, with Bedrock and Vertex routes. Eleven open issues show gaps: Vertex drops cache_control (#3401, 2026-04-23), .jpg is sent as image/jpg and rejected (#1292), cachedInputTokens is null for streamed Bedrock Anthropic calls (#2780), and the Go client panics on Anthropic-style system arrays (#3486). Issue #2673 (2025-10-29) asks for the Claude Code CLI as a client type, and the earlier #2229 was closed without response. BAML clients are raw API calls. No mode drives a Claude Code session, so BAML cannot stand in for agent() in our Workflow scripts.
cards.evidence: Issue titles and short bodies, each reported by one user. The search shows 11 matches, all relayed through the fetch tool. No maintainer replies were visible.
cards.first_guess: Settles whether BAML could sit under the orchestration layer: it cannot, because our agents are Claude Code subagents with tools, not API completions. The sweep's value is ideas only.

cards.source_title: Issue #5499: Local tracing records custom client headers (plain text in CAS, unsalted sha256 in network span)
cards.quote: Local tracing records custom client headers
cards.claim: Telemetry and tracing in the v1 toolchain deserve scrutiny before any trial. TELEMETRY.md says anonymous usage data is collected and excludes prompts, responses and keys. It is opt-out (`baml telemetry disable` or DO_NOT_TRACK=1), and the page does not say outright that it is on by default. Issue #5499 reports that the local trace store keeps custom header values in plain text and that the network span stores an unsalted short sha256 of each header, Authorization included. Open issues #5249 and #5309 ask for tracing without prompt bodies, and #5300 reports that the native HTTP transport follows redirects, so a request body can reach a host other than base_url.
cards.evidence: One reporter's inspection of the trace store (state: open, no labels). TELEMETRY.md was read separately and does not address headers or Boundary cloud tracing. The redirect and tracing issues are single reports I did not reproduce.
cards.first_guess: Fits the owner's rule that nothing is installed without a decision. If a trial were ever approved: sandbox only, telemetry disabled, throwaway keys, no cloud tracing. Nothing for the harness now.

notes: Fetch results are digests from WebFetch's small model, so quotes are as relayed and not independently checked. The prior assessment fits BAML v0 (now labelled legacy), not the current canary README, which presents a pre-1.0 general-purpose agent language (v1) with its own VM, tests and ai.Agent loop. Two release lines exist (0.22x changelog; baml-language 0.x nightlies), and I could not establish how they relate. The release and issue list endpoints were too large to page, so cadence rests on CHANGELOG.md. Nothing here argues for adoption. The transferable ideas are in R-05, R-06, R-09 and R-12.
